newsitem.title: UK: British Gas lifted by BP deal.
newsitem.headline: British Gas lifted by BP deal.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc were indicated higher on Thursday after it said it had reached agreement with British Petroleum Co Plc over arrangements under which it was under contract to buy gas at uneconomic prices.
British Gas shares were indicated 7p higher at 221p in pre-market business while BP shed 4p to 679 1/2p.

Under the deal, BP will receive compensating payments in return for giving British Gas relief on volumes of gas it must lift and on price. British Gas said it had agreed to pay total compensation of 293 million pounds.
"I'm not sure I can be ecstatic about British Gas having to pay out 293 million, though I expect people will be happy to see some progress,' said one trader.
British Gas has so-called "take-or-pay' contracts with other suppliers apart from BP and analysts were hopeful that it could strike more deals.
"This puts pressure on other energy companies to follow BP and to come to some sensible arrangement with British Gas,' said Bruce Evers of Henderson Crosthwaite.
British Gas chairman Richard Giordano told Reuters there could be "one or two' more deals announced in the near future with gas suppliers.
